[LEXP.8.8.2] **A right-hand side with no value is not foldable.** An operation
has no value to fold to when the engine would raise a fault evaluating it, or
when its `Float` result is NaN ([LDET.3.6.2]). The compiler must refuse, with
`DS_VALIDATE_CONST_NOT_FOLDABLE`, a `const` whose right-hand side contains such
an operation, whether or not the rest of the expression would absorb its result:
an `Int` zero divisor ([LEXP.7.15.1]), a negative shift count ([LEXP.7.14.1]), a
`Float` to `Int` conversion of a value with no `Int` ([LCST.4.5.2]), or
a `calendar` call that raises ([LTIM.14.3]).

A `const` holds a value, and `null` is the absence of one ([LNUL.2.1]). The
compiler must refuse, with the same code and under any annotation, a `const`
whose right-hand side contains `null` or a fallible `::T?` conversion
([LCST.4.5.2]).

An operation that another clause
refuses over constant operands keeps that clause's code ([LEXP.3.7.4],
[LEXP.4.2], [LEXP.7.8], [LEXP.10.2.2], [LINT.7.4]), so a `const` refuses a text
as a rule does. `1 // 0` is [LEXP.10.2.2]'s and `1 << -1` is [LEXP.7.8]'s, in a
`const` and in a rule alike. `1 // (1 - 1)`, which no other clause refuses, is
this clause's.
